full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the provisions of Section 19(2) (3) (4) and (5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 putting an embargo on entertainment of an application under Section 19(1) unless 10% of the decreetal dues is deposited in the Court passing the decree shall not be declared to be void being ultra vires the provisions of Article 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution why Judgment and Order dated 18-4-2005 (Annexure-C) passed by respondent No. 2 in Artha Rin Suit No. 104 of 2004 shall not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal, effect. 

 2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that respondent No. 3-Janata Bank Amir Market Branch, Chittagong as plaintiff instituted the suit before the respondent No. 2 Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong against the petitioner for realization of loan money and the suit was registered as Artha Rin Suit No. 104 of 2004. The petitioner herein appeared in the suit and submitted written statement denying material averments of the plaint. Ultimately the suit was decreed exparte against the defendants-petitioner on 18-4-2005 and the decree was drawn up and signed on 24-4-2005. Pursuant to that Decree Execution Case No. 288 of 2005 started and 14-6-2006 was fixed for auction sale but on that date auction could not be held and next date was fixed on 13-7-2006 for the same (Annexure-D). It is at this stage the petitioner moved this Division and on 12-7-2006 obtained the present Rule and stay mainly challenging the vires of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain). 

 5. In elaborating his submissions Mr Kabir contends that Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special law making special provisions overriding all other provisions of law and section 19 of Ain bears an implication as the legislature in its wisdom thought it appropriate and proper to be in the manner as it is there in the Ain. He also submits that at the time of institution of the suit the petitioner as defendant entered appearance by filing written statement but subsequently the suit was decreed exparte subsequent to which date was fixed for auction sale on 13-7-2006 but the petitioner with full knowledge right thereafter moved this petition without taking recourse to section 19 of the Ain for setting-aside the exparte decree. This, as he submits, is cunning device only to frustrate the Artha Rin Proceeding before the Adalat. 

 8. In the decision of Korea Bangladesh Food Products Ltd vs National Bank. Ltd 13 MLR (AD) 253 the Appellate Division in the context of section 41 of Ain held that appeal against order passed in Execution Case of Artha Rin Adalat without deposit of 10% is not maintainable. In that case in execution proceeding the order was challenged without depositing 10% of the decreetal amount and the Appellate Division held the appeal without such deposit is not appeal in the eye of law. We induct the same principle and hold this principle is applicable in case of filing any application under section 19 of Ain that is to say that any application is competent under section 19 if it is filed with 10% of deposit as required under the said section. The said provision cannot be said to be violative of fundamental right of the petitioner guaranteed by Article 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution. 

 9. Provisions of Special law cannot be challenged by bringing some fallacious and frivolous argument on the pretext of violation of some rights under the Constitution admittedly when the same is bereft of any sense whatsoever. The suit was filed in the year 2004 and decreed exparte and Execution Case proceeded up to 2006. Thereafter due to order of stay by this Division Execution Case could not proceed for the last six years. This sort of exercise of the petitioner by bringing a frivolous application is absolutely unhealthy which was discard and deprecate.
